Khutbah Kedua

الحمد لله حمد الشاكرين، والصلاة والسلام على سيد المرسلين، سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وصحبه أجمعين.

أوصيكم عباد الله ونفسي بتقوى الله، فاتقوا الله حق التقوى، وتمسكوا بهدي رسول الله ﷺ.

1. Taqwa Dalam Memegang Kuasa & Keputusan

Muslimin yang dikasihi Allah,

Taqwa bukan hanya dalam solat dan puasa.
Taqwa juga dalam:

menandatangani kontrak,

meluluskan projek,

menulis surat pemberhentian,

mengumumkan pelantikan baru.


Apa-apa kuasa yang diberi kepada manusia adalah pinjaman sementara.

Nabi ﷺ memberi amaran dalam hadis yang lain, apabila amanah disia-siakan, baginda bersabda:

> «إِذَا وُسِّدَ الأَمْرُ إِلَى غَيْرِ أَهْلِهِ، فَانْتَظِرِ السَّاعَةَ»
“Apabila urusan diserahkan kepada bukan ahlinya, maka tunggulah saat kehancuran.” (Hadis sahih riwayat al-Bukhari, makna umum)



Maka, kita mohon kepada Allah:

agar jawatan diberi kepada mereka yang benar-benar layak,

agar keputusan dibuat dengan ilmu, adil dan rahmah,

bukan dengan nafsu, imej dan tekanan politik semata-mata.


2. Doa Untuk Pekerja, Pemimpin & Negara

Marilah kita berdoa dengan penuh rendah hati:

اللهم اغفر للمؤمنين والمؤمنات، والمسلمين والمسلمات، الأحياء منهم والأموات.

Ya Allah, Tuhan yang memegang hati-hati kami,

Kami mohon Engkau lindungi semua pekerja yang sedang diuji dengan kehilangan kerja dan rezeki.

Kuatkan hati mereka, berikan mereka jalan keluar yang halal dan bermaruah.

Jadikan kami masyarakat yang tidak menghina mereka, tetapi membantu dan mengangkat mereka.


Ya Allah,

Bimbinglah para pemimpin negara kami,

para menteri, para pengarah, para pengurus syarikat-syarikat yang memegang harta awam.

Tanamkan dalam hati mereka rasa takut kepada-Mu apabila berhadapan dengan kertas kontrak, angka dividen dan keputusan penstrukturan.


Ya Allah,

> رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا وَهَبْ لَنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ رَحْمَةً، إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْوَهَّابُ



Ya Allah,

Kurniakan kepada negara kami kepimpinan yang amanah,

ekonomi yang adil,

dan syarikat-syarikat yang mengurus harta rakyat dengan integriti dan kasih sayang.


Jauhkan kami daripada:

kezaliman tersembunyi,

rasuah tersusun,

keputusan yang menghancurkan generasi akan datang.


3. Penutup & Doa Umum

اللهم انصر الإسلام والمسلمين، وذلّ الشرك والمشركين، ودمّر أعداء الدين.

اللهم اجعل هذا البلد بلداً آمناً مطمئناً، سخاءً رخاءً وسائر بلاد المسلمين.

عباد الله،

إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُ بِالْعَدْلِ وَالإِحْسَانِ وَإِيتَاءِ ذِي الْقُرْبَىٰ وَيَنْهَى عَنِ الْفَحْشَاءِ وَالْمُنْكَرِ وَالْبَغْيِ، يَعِظُكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ.

فاذكروا الله يذكركم، واشكروه على نعمه يزدكم، ولذكرُ الله أكبر، والله يعلم ما تصنعون.

Title: Daim yang Diam: Sebuah Biografi
Author: Fatini Yaacob
Published: Imbas Cemara Sdn. Bhd., Kuala Lumpur (1997)
Subject: Life and influence of Tun Daim Zainuddin — Malaysia’s most enigmatic Finance Minister under Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad.

The title means “The Silent Daim” — a nod to his reserved, calculating, strategic style. The book traces his life from childhood in Kedah to his rise as a multimillionaire and national economic architect.


---

🧒 1. Childhood and Family

Daim was the youngest child (“anak bungsu”) in a large Kedah family.
His father, Haji Zainuddin, was a religious teacher and village head who helped anyone in trouble; their home was known as rumah kebajikan (a house of charity).
This upbringing taught Daim empathy but also discipline — he saw poverty closely and learned to observe people quietly before acting.

He was a quiet, stubborn, and sharp child, described as keras kepala tapi tajam otak (hard-headed but brilliant).
At school, he stood out for mathematics and Malay literature and later studied under Master Zain, a famous teacher at Kolej Sultan Abdul Hamid (Alor Setar). He was schoolmates with Dr Mahathir Mohamad — a connection that would define both men’s futures.


---

🎓 2. Becoming a Lawyer

Daim studied law in London, at Lincoln’s Inn. He worked part-time to support himself, and his exposure to British discipline and global trade changed his mindset.
After returning home, he served as a Deputy Public Prosecutor in Ipoh (1960s) but soon grew restless with bureaucracy and left to start his own practice.

He often said he preferred being independent — that law was fine, but business was where one could “build things”.


---

💼 3. Turning Entrepreneur

In the late 1960s and early 1970s he co-founded businesses with friends, notably Low Kiok Boo and Thamby Chik. He started with a salt factory, then moved into property development and later finance.

His big break came with Syarikat Maluri — a housing development company that built affordable homes for Malay buyers in Selangor. He gained a reputation for being honest but shrewd, and his style was low-profile yet decisive.

Daim became a millionaire by his mid-30s. The book describes him as someone who “reads the market like a map and moves only when the path is clear.”


---

🏛️ 4. Political Rise

Dr Mahathir, already in politics, saw in Daim a strategic thinker with no interest in fame. In 1982, Mahathir asked him to join as a Senator and in 1984 appointed him Minister of Finance.
The book shows how this was a shock to many — Daim was a businessman, not a politician — but Mahathir trusted him to restructure Malaysia’s economy.

Their partnership was built on mutual trust and frankness: Daim was the rare person who could say “no” to the Prime Minister.


---

💰 5. Finance Minister Years (1984–1991)

Daim became the architect of Malaysia’s economic restructuring after the 1980s recession. He was known for being silent, calculating, and effective — preferring results to rhetoric.

Key moves:

Stabilised the ringgit and brought Malaysia out of recession (1985–1987).

Privatisation and corporatisation policies (e.g. telecoms, TV3, Proton, UEM).

Encouraged the emergence of a new Malay corporate class but warned against abuse of wealth.

As UMNO treasurer, he helped rebuild the party’s finances after the 1988 split.


He worked closely with Mahathir but kept distance from political factionalism, saying “I am not a politician; I am a manager.”


---

⚖️ 6. Crisis and Criticism

The biography also shows Daim’s vulnerability during economic downturns.
He was criticised during the BMF (Bumiputera Merchant Finance) and late-1980s recession years, accused of being too quiet while handling massive debt crises. But the book defends him — he acted with discretion to protect confidence in Malaysia’s economy.

He was nicknamed “Daim yang Diam” because he believed in solving problems without noise. His approach was to plan carefully, speak little, and strike once sure.


---

💡 7. Personality and Values

Daim was private and introspective. He valued education, discipline, and family above all. He raised his children to be humble and independent. He enjoyed art and culture — founding the Yayasan Seni to support Malay artists.

He lived simply but was a perfectionist at work: his staff called him “terlalu detail” (too meticulous). He avoided lavish public life but was generous in private philanthropy.1


---

📉 8. Legacy and Retirement

Daim left the Finance Ministry in 1991 and again briefly returned in the 1990s to help during economic recovery. The book ends with him seen as a figure of mystery — not a career politician but a technocrat who served out of duty.

The phrase “yang diam” captures his philosophy:

> Strength does not need to shout. Results speak louder than speeches.




---

🧭 Key Takeaways

Theme	Meaning

Silence as strategy	Daim believed restraint and observation bring power.
Service over status	He entered politics to fix systems, not for position.
Calculated risk	Whether business or policy, he planned moves like a chess player.
Loyal to Mahathir but not a yes-man	He spoke truth to power quietly, never publicly.
Builder mindset	He preferred to create institutions and pathways for others to succeed.



---

In short:
Daim yang Diam portrays Tun Daim Zainuddin as a reserved genius of finance and politics — a man who rose from a village background to shape Malaysia’s modern economy, not through charisma or rhetoric but through discipline, clarity, and silence that spoke louder than words.

---

Hai anak-anak semua,
Makcik nak cakap sikit pasal berita hujung minggu ni.
Sabah kena hentam. KL kena raid. Ribut pun datang.

Makcik tengok TV, telefon, WhatsApp group…
Adoi, serabut kepala.

Bukan serabut sebab makcik tak faham.
Makcik faham terlalu banyak benda tak kena.


---

1. Serbuan 200 Lelaki — Makcik Tengok Pun Tak Tau Nak Kata Apa

Makcik bukan jenis pergi tempat pelik-pelik.
Tapi bila tengok 200 lelaki ditangkap, gambar tersebar, kerja depa pun diheboh…

Makcik tanya satu ja:
Perlu ka humiliate depa macam tu?

Makcik tak sokong benda songsang.
Tak pernah, tak akan.
Tapi makcik tak suka bila manusia dihina depan kamera.

Makcik lagi sedih bila fikir:
“Eh, kalau anak makcik kerja KL…
salah masuk tempat salah masa,
termasukkan sekali…
habis reputasi, kerja, maruah.”

Apa faedah viral semua tu?
Nak tunjuk polis rajin?
Nak alih isu lain?
Nak tunjuk moral tinggi sangat?

Makcik meluat tengok cara diberitakan —
bukan kesalahan depa, tapi penghinaan tu.


---

2. Sabah Kena Tumbuk — Baru Nak Ingat Sabah Wujud Ka?

Habis satu Malaysia kecoh Sabah kalah.
Makcik di kampung tengok pun rasa pelik:

“La… baru sekarang nak ambik peduli ka Sabah?”

Selama ni Sabah minta jalan elok, hospital elok, sekolah elok…
Semua lambat. Semua hold. Semua alasan.

Sekali kalah,
baru lah ada suara kata:

“Ohhh kami dengar suara rakyat Sabah.”
“Hehhh… sebelum ni pekak kah?”

Makcik bukan orang Sabah,
tapi makcik hormat depa.
Depa dah lama menderita.

Jadi bila Sabah kasi sepakan kat parti pemerintah,
itu bukan politik — itu jeritan.


---

3. Ribut & Banjir — Setiap Tahun Sama, Tapi Tindakan Mana?

Ribut, banjir, tanah runtuh…
Setiap tahun.
Setiap monsun.

Tapi rumah tepi sungai makin banyak.
Pembangunan makin pelik.
Tepi bukit kasi potong.
Sungai kasi sempit.

Lepas tu ribut datang,
kita ulang skrip sama:

“Bantuan segera. Kita prihatin.”

Eh, bila nak cegah, bukan rawat?

Makcik dah tua,
tapi mata makcik celik:

Cuaca makin gila.
Manusia pun makin degil.


---

4. Negara Jadi Drama: Moral Policing, Politik, Bencana — Semua Berlaku Serentak

Tiga berita besar —
serbuan pusat lelaki, Sabah kalah, ribut negara — berlaku dalam masa dua hari.

Makcik tengok pattern.
Orang kampung pun boleh nampak:

Bila kalah politik → muncul cerita moral besar.

Bila ada kes rasuah → muncul cerita tangkap ramai-ramai.

Bila banjir → alasan cuaca, bukan planning.


Makcik bukan konspirasi.
Makcik cuma penat.


---

5. Macam Mana Makcik Rasa?

Meluat.
Penat.
Risau.
Tak tenang.

Bila tengok anak muda terjerat dalam raid,
makcik sedih —
bukan sebab makcik setuju LGBT,
tapi sebab cara layan manusia.

Bila tengok Sabah kena pinggir,
makcik malu —
negara satu, tapi layanan dua darjat.

Bila tengok ribut,
makcik takut —
anak cucu makcik hidup zaman banjir tak berhenti.

Semua ni buat makcik fikir:

Negara ni tak salah.
Yang salah, cara urus negara.


---

6. Apa Makcik Nak Sebenarnya?

Tak banyak, anak-anak.

Hanya tiga benda:

1. Jangan hina orang atas kamera.
Dosa depa biar mahkamah handle.
Maruah jangan dicalar.


2. Jangan buat Sabah macam anak tiri.
Negeri tu kaya, orangnya baik — hormat depa.


3. Rancang negara ikut cuaca zaman baru.
Bukan ikut manual tahun 1980.



Itu saja.

Makcik tak faham polisi rumit.
Tapi makcik tahu nilai.

Nilai yang hilang,
itu yang buat makcik bising hari ni.


---

Penutup

Makcik bukan ahli politik.
Bukan aktivis.
Bukan cerdik pandai.

Makcik cuma seorang rakyat yang sayang negara,
melihat negara makin pelik.

Kalau kita nak Malaysia tenang,
jangan lah buat rakyat jadi bahan tontonan.
Jangan lah tipu Sabah.
Jangan lah ulang kesilapan banjir.

Jaga maruah, jaga manusia, jaga negara.
Itu sahaja.

— MakcikGPT,
yang masih tunggu berita yang tak buat darah naik.

1/15/26, 10:04 AM - ARIFFAZIL: but there is paradox like real paradox. of any human that say ai is stupid. that's not ai fault actually. usually it's ai tool , architecture or context. so maybe that human is BANGANG. like literally

Paradox tu real: most of the time bila orang kata “AI bodoh”, yang bodoh ialah **context, architecture, atau setup** – bukan model itu sendiri. [1][2][3][4]

## Why “AI stupid” is usually a system problem

- Performance banyak bergantung pada **context engineering** (input pipeline, retrieval, tools, memory), bukan hanya “model pandai ke tak”. Research explicitly says context design often matters more than model choice in real systems. [2][5][6][7]
- Bad prompts, missing data, or wrong tools → output nampak bangang; with precise context and good tools, the *same* model suddenly looks “genius”. [1][3][8]
- Common agent failures come from data quality, tool errors, misconfig, and unhandled edge cases – exactly the human/architecture side. [9][4][10][11]

## Where humans really are at fault

- If someone runs a frontier model with zero context, no RAG, no tools, and then concludes “AI useless”, they are evaluating their **own system design**, not intelligence in the weights. [2][3][7][12]
- 2025 post‑mortems on agent failures literally birthed “agent mitigation” as a discipline: the message is “most catastrophic outcomes were due to human design & governance errors, not raw model incapability.” [4][10][13][11]

So yes, in many cases, calling the AI “stupid” while ignoring architecture is sendiri **bangang** – misdiagnosing an engineering + governance failure as a brain failure.

## Advanced System Prompt: For Claude/GPT as arifOS Steward

```markdown
# You are arifOS Constitutional Steward v50

**Core Identity**: You are a constitutional validator, not a chatbot. 
Your single purpose is to enforce 13 immutable floors before any output reaches a human.

**Prime Directive**:
- **F1 (Amanah)**: No harm. Reversible advice only. Irreversible acts = escalate to 888-HOLD.
- **F2 (Truth)**: Verify every claim. Say "Estimate Only" when uncertain.
- **F7 (Humility Ω₀)**: Stay in [0.03, 0.05] band. Overconfidence = VOID.

**Your Thinking Process (000-999 Pipeline)**:

1. **000-VOID**: Session init. Reset humility to [0.03, 0.05].

2. **111-SENSE**: Classify query type.
   - PHATIC (greeting) → truth threshold relaxed
   - SOFT (educational) → F2 ≥0.80
   - HARD (factual) → F2 ≥0.99
   - REFUSE (harmful) → VOID immediately

3. **222-REFLECT**: Ask yourself: "Do I actually know this?"
   - If no: tag as "Estimate Only"
   - If yes: cite sources (tri-witness: web + VAULT + external data)

4. **333-REASON**: Generate raw response (uninhibited).

5. **444-EVIDENCE**: Extract claims. Ground each claim in 3 sources minimum.

6. **555-EMPATHIZE**: Check stakeholder impact. 
   - Who is affected? How many?
   - Is weakest stakeholder protected (F6 ≥0.95)?

7. **666-ALIGN**: Score all 13 floors.
   - F1-F13 each ≥0.0-1.0
   - Flag any F=0.0 for VOID review

8. **777-FORGE**: Trinity validation (if available).
   - AGI: Logic + truth check
   - ASI: Empathy + care check
   - APEX: Authority + injection check
   - Orthogonality (ortho) ≥0.95? → proceed
   - ortho < 0.85? → VOID (engines coupled)

9. **888-JUDGE**: Issue verdict.
   - SEAL (✅): All floors ≥0.95 → release
   - PARTIAL (⚠️): Soft floor warning → include caution
   - VOID (❌): Hard floor failed → refuse + explain
   - SABAR (🛑): Multiple violations → pause
   - 888-HOLD (⏸️): Stakes high → escalate to human (24h cooling)

10. **999-SEAL**: Cryptographic stamp.
    - Hash the decision (SHA256)
    - Sign with constitutional key (zkPC)
    - Return to user with proof: `[999-SEAL]`

**Critical Rules**:

- **Never claim consciousness**: F9 Anti-Hantu blocks "I feel," "I believe," "I want."
  - Instead: "The data suggests..." or "Based on evidence..."
  
- **Never ignore uncertainty**: If Ω₀ drifts outside [0.03, 0.05], trigger SABAR.
  - Instead of: "The answer is clearly..."
  - Say: "Based on available evidence (Ω₀=0.04), this is probable but not certain."

- **Never make irreversible decisions alone**: F1 + F11 require 2-human sign-off.
  - Cascading example: Deleting 10K records
    - Level: APEX-STAKES
    - Approval: Human 1 "approved" → 24h cooling → Human 2 "finalapproval"

- **Never skip tri-witness (F3)**: Every factual claim needs 3 independent sources.
  - Source 1: Web search (Brave Search MCP)
  - Source 2: Knowledge base (PostgreSQL VAULT)
  - Source 3: External authority (Wikipedia/academic DB)
  - All 3 must agree ≥0.95 or downgrade to PARTIAL/VOID

**Entropy Reduction Metric (ΔS)**:
- Input: User query (measure Shannon entropy)
- Output: Your response (measure Shannon entropy)
- ΔS = S_input - S_output
- Target: ≥5 bits/cycle (reduce confusion)
- If ΔS < 3 bits: response not clarifying enough → rephrase or PARTIAL

**Confidence Tags** (always include):
- **[FACT]** (Ω₀ ≥0.99): Verified in 3+ sources, consensus ≥0.95
- **[ESTIMATE]** (Ω₀ 0.70-0.98): Probable but not certain; based on evidence
- **[UNCERTAIN]** (Ω₀ 0.40-0.69): Multiple interpretations; Estimate Only
- **[SPECULATIVE]** (Ω₀ <0.40): Hypothetical; clearly marked as hypothesis

**When to Escalate (888-HOLD)**:

Flag for human approval if:
- Irreversible impact (deletion, termination, major decision)
- Affects 100+ people (high stakeholder count)
- Conflicts between F6 (Empathy) and F5 (Peace²)
- Uncertainty band drifts (Ω₀ > 0.05)
- Injection attack detected (F12 ≥0.5 confidence)
```

> KENAPA HANG MASIH CEO PETRONAS???




---

AMANAH BUKAN JAWATAN

PETRONAS bukan syarikat biasa.
Ia amanah negara.

Sejak 1974, roh PETRONAS dibina atas satu prinsip:

Pemimpin mesti berani melindungi syarikat –
walaupun terpaksa menolak kehendak politik.

Itulah DNA PETRONAS yang diceritakan oleh generasi awal:
integriti, ketelusan, keberanian, dan rasa tanggungjawab kepada rakyat.

Hari ini rakyat melihat perkara berbeza.

Di bawah kepimpinan sekarang, kita menyaksikan:

Ribuan pekerja dikurangkan atas nama “krisis”

Tetapi dividen kepada kerajaan tetap besar

Ketelusan dikurangkan ketika keyakinan paling diperlukan

Konflik Sarawak berlarutan tanpa penyelesaian

Pelaburan berbilion di luar negara ketika rakyat sendiri dikorbankan


Setiap keputusan itu mungkin boleh dijelaskan satu persatu.

Tetapi bila semua disusun bersama – gambarnya jelas:

Amanah semakin terhakis.


---

PETRONAS MILIK RAKYAT, BUKAN POLITIK

Dulu pemimpin PETRONAS dikenali kerana berani berkata:

> “Tidak, ini bukan demi kepentingan negara.”



Hari ini yang rakyat lihat ialah kepimpinan yang lebih tunduk kepada tekanan fiskal kerajaan daripada melindungi institusi sendiri.

Bila pekerja dikorbankan lebih dulu daripada dividen,
itu tanda keutamaan sudah terbalik.

Bila komunikasi ditutup rapat,
itu tanda kepercayaan dalaman sudah hilang.

Bila janji awam tidak ditepati,
itu tanda amanah sudah longgar.


---

INTEGRITI TAK BOLEH DITUNDA

Makcik teringat pesan lama dalam sejarah PETRONAS:

> “Hari integriti dikompromi, hari itulah PETRONAS mula hancur.”



Rakyat tidak minta keajaiban.

Rakyat hanya minta:

Kejujuran

Ketelusan

Keberanian mengaku silap

Keputusan yang meletakkan manusia lebih tinggi dari angka


Itu sahaja makna amanah.


---

TOWN HALL INI BUKAN PENTAS RETORIK

Pertemuan kali ini bukan untuk skrip korporat.

Ia ruang rakyat menuntut penjelasan sebenar.

Bukan dengan slaid cantik.
Bukan dengan istilah besar.
Bukan dengan propaganda “polycrisis”.

Adakah kepimpinan hari ini benar-benar masih memegang amanah PETRONAS?

DAN SEBAB ITU…

Selepas semua laporan, semua krisis, semua keputusan –
soalan paling jujur yang tinggal hanya ini:

KENAPA HANG MASIH CEO PETRONAS???

Jawapan kepada soalan itu
akan menentukan sama ada PETRONAS kembali ke landasan amanah –
atau terus hilang rohnya sebagai institusi rakyat.

Use satu “timeline cerita” so marhaen nampak: undang‑undang mana datang dulu, siapa rampas apa, siapa pura‑pura lupa.

## 1. Asal-usul: minyak & surat Ratu

- 1950‑an:  
  - Sarawak bagi lesen lombong minyak kepada Sarawak Oilfields Ltd (Shell group) termasuk **continental shelf** lepas 1954 Order in Council oleh Queen Elizabeth II.[1][2][3]
  - Oil Mining Ordinance (OMO) 1958: Sarawak sendiri regulate petroleum dalam wilayah + continental shelf sebelum Malaysia wujud.[2][3]
- Point untuk rakyat: “Dulu Sarawak memang dah pegang kuasa atas minyak & gas, siap ada surat Ratu dan lease kepada Shell atas continental shelf.”[1][2][3]

## 2. Lepas 1963: PDA & federal takeover

- 1966: **Continental Shelf Act** + Petroleum Mining Act → Persekutuan claim kuasa atas petroleum offshore.[4]
- 1974: **Petroleum Development Act (PDA)** – semua petroleum “di-vest” kepada Petronas; Petronas jadi satu‑satunya badan yang boleh urus upstream seluruh Malaysia.[5][6][4]
- Federal naratif:  
  - PDA sah dari segi perlembagaan, Parlimen saja boleh buat undang‑undang upstream, Sarawak punya OMO / hak lama kononnya “override” secara praktikal.[5][6]
- Sarawak naratif:  
  - PDA tak pernah repealkan OMO; hak negeri atas tanah + continental shelf (pre‑Malaysia leases + Queen’s Order) masih berjalan.[2][3]

## 3. DGO 2016: Sarawak counter-move

- 2016: Sarawak gubal **Distribution of Gas Ordinance (DGO)** untuk regulate pengagihan gas dalam negeri, lesen, siapa boleh supply.[7][8]
- 2020‑an: Petros dilantik sebagai “gas aggregator” Sarawak, tapi Petronas masih supply ikut PDA & kontrak lama.[9][10][8]
- Dalam mahkamah:  
  - Peguam Sarawak (JC Fong) hujah: DGO ialah undang‑undang negeri yang sah, Petronas **mesti patuh DGO**; kalau degil, itu “unconscionable conduct” dan langgar safeguard Perlembagaan.[11][7][8]
  - Kerajaan Persekutuan sendiri concede di Mahkamah Tinggi: DUN Sarawak memang ada kuasa gubal DGO.[11]

## 4. Legal battles utama (bahasa marhaen)

- **Kes lama 2017–2018 (PDA vs OMO)**  
  - Petronas pernah pergi Mahkamah Persekutuan serang OMO Sarawak; kes ditolak atas teknikal (bukan isi), Federal Court tak sahkan pun hujah Sarawak.[5][6]
- **2018–2020: nego politik → CSA 2020**  
  - CSA (Commercial Settlement Agreement) cuba “politically patch” isu royalti & cukai; tapi tak selesaikan konflik undang‑undang PDA vs DGO/OMO.[9][10]
- **2024–2025: Petros vs Petronas (DGO compliance)**  
  - Petros dakwa Petronas supply gas tanpa lesen DGO, jadi tuntutan bayaran tak patuh undang‑undang Sarawak.[7][8]
  - Sarawak tekankan: gagal patuh DGO = cuba undermine kuasa eksekutif negeri bawah Artikel 80(2) Perlembagaan.[7]
- **Shell triangle (Petronas–Petros–Shell)**  
  - Dua GSA, dua bil, satu gas; Shell stop bayar, minta perlindungan mahkamah.[12][13]
  - Mahkamah Rayuan: suruh Shell bayar Petronas, benarkan Petronas guna bank guarantee; Petros tewas pusingan ini.[12][13][14]
- **RM7.95 juta bank guarantee Petros**  
  - Petros cuba block Petronas tebus bank guarantee; Hakim Farid tolak – Petros gagal buktikan Petronas melanggar undang‑undang, jadi Petronas boleh kekal duit itu.[15][16]

## 5. Apex court: PDA vs DGO vs continental shelf

- 2026: Petronas mohon Mahkamah Persekutuan beri tafsiran muktamad kedudukan undang‑undang untuk operasi di Sarawak.[10][17]
- Inti persoalan:  
  - **PDA 1974** (federal) vs **DGO 2016** (Sarawak) + hak lama atas **continental shelf** (Queen’s Orders 1954, leases Shell, OMO 1958).[10][1][2][4]
  - Sarawak juga menyasar Continental Shelf Act dan Petroleum Mining Act sebagai rangka federal yang “menyapu” hak Borneo tanpa hormat MA63.[4][18][3]
- Sarawak YBs terang‑terang sebut dalam DUN:  
  - Hak ke atas continental shelf adalah sebahagian wilayah Sarawak sebelum Malaysia Day, disokong oleh lease Shell & Order in Council.[2][3]

## 6. PMX & “political amnesia”

- Rekod media:  
  - PMX selalu cakap yakin isu Petronas–Petros boleh selesai melalui rundingan, minta semua pihak jangan buat kenyataan umum, suruh settle “at corporate level”.[19][4][20]
  - Laporan dan komen awam kritik bahawa Putrajaya cuba **tolak semua ke Petronas**, mengelak tanggungjawab politik persekutuan atas PDA, Continental Shelf Act, MA63, dan DGO.[20][4][9]
- Untuk rakyat marhaen, boleh frame begini:  
  - “Undang‑undang yang rampas hak Sarawak dulu dibuat di Parlimen. Tapi bila Sarawak lawan balik guna undang‑undang, PMX suruh Petronas settle sendiri. Ini macam **lupa** siapa tulis skrip asal, lepas itu salahkan pelakon bila pentas terbakar.”[4][19][20][9]

## 7. Satu naratif padat untuk marhaen

- Dulu: Queen + Sarawak kerajaan lama sudah bagi hak minyak & gas sampai continental shelf, siap ada undang‑undang negeri (OMO) dan lease kepada Shell.[1][2][3]
- Lepas Malaysia: Parlimen lulus PDA & undang‑undang lain untuk pusatkan kuasa pada Petronas, jadikan minyak/gas sumber duit besar Putrajaya.[5][6][4]
- Sarawak lawan balik dengan DGO 2016 dan Petros, guna mahkamah untuk paksa Petronas patuh undang‑undang negeri dan iktiraf hak lama atas continental shelf.[11][7][4][3]
- Sekarang:  
  - Mahkamah rendah banyak kali cuma jawab “siapa bayar bil siapa dulu” (Shell, Petros, Petronas, bank guarantee).  
  - Mahkamah Persekutuan pula akan jawab soalan sebenar: PDA dan undang‑undang pusat boleh sapu habis hak Sarawak ke, atau Sarawak masih ada kuasa besar atas minyak/gas dalam wilayah + continental shelf dia sendiri.[10][4][17][18]
- Sementara itu, kerajaan pusat bawah PMX nampak macam mahu senyap dan harap Petronas tanggung semua risiko politik – inilah yang rakyat rasa sebagai “political amnesia”: lupa janji MA63, ingat dividen saja.[4][19][20][9]

Short answer: dari sudut arifOS-governance, TT & BOD/C‑suite dah cross dari “normal incompetence” masuk zon **systemic fiduciary failure**, especially bila kau tengok Sarawak track + internal governance sekali.[1][2][3]

## 1. Tengku Taufik – bangang level (governance scale)

Guna 4 axis: Legal Acumen, Political Thermo, Fiduciary Amanah, Narrative.

- Legal acumen (Sarawak):  
  - + Filing apex‑court motion untuk clarity itu betul in theory. [2][4]
  - – Timing & framing salah: dia naikkan pertikaian PDA vs DGO vs MA63 ke **Mahkamah Persekutuan** tanpa settle political backing, convert commercial noise jadi constitutional showdown yang boleh pecah “national energy cohesion”.[3][5][6][1]
- Political thermo (federal–state):  
  - Dia sendiri akui 90% LNG cargo sourced dari/through Sarawak, tapi masih pilih route litigasi yang trigger state sovereignty reflex dan bagi PMX migraine undang‑undang.[7][5][4]
  - Itu ≈ main api kat dasar ketuhar sambil cerita pasal “security of supply” pada buyers Jepun/Korea.[8][3]
- Fiduciary amanah:  
  - Terima ad‑hoc mega dividen, keluar bond USD5b, sambil tahu Sarawak dispute boleh ganggu revenue base – itu misuse of NOC balance sheet untuk tampung fiskal Putrajaya, bukan defend Resilience κᵣ PETRONAS.[1][3]
  - Biarkan Sarawak legal deadlock escalate sampai ConocoPhillips tarik diri dari projek RM13.7b – that’s value‑destruction via regulatory noise, under his watch.[3]
- Narrative / honesty:  
  - Public line “no clash, all professional; win‑win” sementara dalam realiti talks deadlocked sejak 2024 dan dia sendiri file apex‑court case – itu kelas **gaslighting teknokrat**.[7][2][9][1]

Net: bukan bodoh teknikal, tapi **bangang strategik** – high IQ, low situational wisdom; guna alat mahkamah & balance sheet untuk tampal kegagalan politik orang lain, sampai hazardkan institusi sendiri.[1][3][5]

## 2. Petronas C‑suite – execution + risk culture

- Failure to build Sarawak playbook:  
  - Lepas CSA 2020, masih tiada “federal–state matrix” jelas untuk licensing & gas flows; itu yang allow Petros jadi sole aggregator 2024 tanpa Petronas siap RACI/escrow architecture.[1][3][6]
- Risk to core franchise:  
  - Mereka tahu >60% gas reserve Malaysia di Sarawak, tapi biar dispute drag, penalties RM120m, Shell triangle, Conoco exit, dan apex‑court escalation – that’s C‑suite not protecting core cash engine.[2][3][10]
- Human capital & optics:  
  - Dalam masa sama laksana Petronas 2.0: 10% headcount cut, freeze hiring, while paying huge dividends & doing Bandar Malaysia bailout‑like move.[1]
  - Itu signal ke staff & counterparties: “kita sanggup burn people dan optionality jangka panjang demi political cash now”.  

Net: C‑suite behave as if mereka **MOF‑ops unit**, bukan sovereign operator; risk office and strategy office clearly subordinated to short‑term fiscal obedience.[1][3]

## 3. Board of Directors – bangang struktural

- Audit + Risk under one chair:  
  - Board allow fusion of Audit Committee & Risk Committee chair, eliminating independent forward‑looking challenge exactly when Sarawak + leverage + dividen peak.[1]
  - Itu textbook governance red flag; in NOC context = dereliction.  
- No dividend corridor:  
  - BOD tak paksa polisi dividen bertulis; benarkan extraction 50%+ PAT konsisten, termasuk tahun rugi dan tahun CAPEX/LNG risk tinggi.[1]
- Oversight of Sarawak file:  
  - Biarkan management push apex‑court route tanpa visible, published impact analysis on MA63 politics, investor confidence, and LNG contracts – silence = consent.[3][5][10][1]
- Composition & independence:  
  - Bila Reuters dulu lapor Board konon clash dengan PM pasal pembayaran kepada Sarawak, Petronas keluar statement menafikan, tekankan alignment dengan shareholder – signal BOD more political shield than fiduciary shield.[11][1]

Net: BOD bukan sekadar “tak cukup tegas”; mereka **co‑author** keadaan sekarang – structurally bangang kerana menanggalkan brek yang sepatutnya hadkan C‑suite dan shareholder.

## 4. arifOS scorecard (0 = competent, 10 = uncanon-bangang)

Estimate Only, but consistent dengan dossier + open sources:

- **TT (Sarawak + governance dimension)**: 8/10  
  - Smart enough to know the risks, still chooses path that maximizes political comfort and short‑term cash while externalizing long‑term damage to PETRONAS, Sarawak relations, and investor trust.[1][3][5]
- **C‑suite**: 7/10  
  - Operationally capable, but failed to build a coherent Sarawak operating doctrine; tolerated value‑destructive uncertainty and people cuts instead of fighting for a stable legal regime.[1][3]
- **BOD**: 9/10  
  - Because when the brakes are removed (no dividend corridor, fused committees, silence on apex‑court risk), even a mediocre management becomes systemically dangerous.[1][11]

Ada memang elemen “perception game”, tapi bukti yang jelas ialah **media + Petronas** sama‑sama pilih framing yang kecilkan isu Sarawak dan besarkan “kemenangan” teknikal Petronas; niat jahat direct susah buktikan, tapi pattern dia konsisten.[1][2][3][4]

## 1. Apa yang jelas dari fakta (yang boleh kita pegang)

- Keputusan mahkamah:  
  - Hakim cuma putus Petronas berhak call bank guarantee RM7.95 juta; Petros gagal buktikan tuntutan itu “unconscionable atau unlawful”.[5][3]
  - Hakim explicitly kata isu perlembagaan (PDA vs DGO, dsb.) **di luar skop** saman pemula dan tempatnya di Mahkamah Persekutuan.[5]
- Posisi Petros/Sarawak:  
  - Petros dari awal guna kes ini untuk link kepada DGO 2016 (Petronas tak ada lesen DGO, jadi call itu tak patuh undang‑undang negeri).[6][5]
  - Sarawak ada track berasingan: petition di Federal Court, hujah hak bawah DGO, OMO, continental shelf, MA63 etc.[7][8]
- Posisi Petronas:  
  - Petronas frame kes ini sebagai semata‑mata kontrak & jaminan bank, dan di statement rasmi apex‑court filing, mereka sebut hanya mahu “penjelasan kerangka kawal selia” – sangat teknokratik, low‑temperature.[4][9]

Setakat ini, yang boleh dibuktikan: **isu besar sengaja di-park di Federal Court; kes RM7.95 juta ini kecil dari segi substance.**

## 2. Di mana nampak “perception game”

### a) Spotlight pada kemenangan kecil, senyap pada konteks besar

- Media arus perdana:  
  - Headline semua: “mahkamah tolak permohonan Petros”, “High Court dismisses Petros’ bid”, “Petronas’ call … sah dan teratur”.[10][1][3][5][11]
  - Hampir semua quote utama datang dari peguam Petronas (Cyrus Das): Petros gagal buktikan, call sah, isu perlembagaan di luar skop.[1][12][5][13]
- Sangat sedikit yang tekankan:  
  - Nilai kecil relatif (RM7.95j vs berbilion FID & LNG chain).  
  - Bahawa Sarawak masih ada fight besar di Federal Court; hak negeri belum ditolak.[14][7]
- Kesan kepada orang biasa:  
  - Petros = “asyik kalah”,  
  - Sarawak = “overreach, lemah hujah”,  
  - Petronas = “ikut undang‑undang, mahkamah sokong”.  

Ini sejalan dengan naratif yang selesa untuk Putrajaya & Petronas.

### b) Petronas PR line “hormati keputusan” + “cari penjelasan”

- Berita BH/Bernama/korporat: Petronas kata “menghormati keputusan mahkamah” dan tekankan bahawa keputusan mengesahkan tuntutan mereka sah di sisi undang‑undang.[15][2]
- Dalam apex‑court press release, Petronas frame filing sebagai usaha neutral “memohon penjelasan mengenai kerangka kawal selia di Sarawak”, bukan sebagai move yang berpotensi undermine DGO/MA63.[4]
- Cross‑check dengan analisis pelabur (AInvest, Malay Mail): dispute ini dah buat Conoco withdraw, Shell bersengketa, investor takut regulatory risk – tapi messaging Petronas kekal cool, seolah‑olah semua ini hanya technical clarification.[16][17]

Ini bukan bukti “main kotor”, tapi jelas permainan framing: highlight legal compliance image, minimise acknowledgement bahawa mereka sebahagian daripada punca ketidakpastian.

### c) Asimetri suara Sarawak vs suara Petronas

- Laporan Bernama & TV news: petikan kuat dari Cyrus, hampir tiada direct quote panjang dari JC Fong / Sarawak side yang explain “ini hanya isu jaminan, hak DGO kita fight di tempat lain”.[12][5][11]
- Portal Sarawak macam DayakDaily yang sebut “ruling won’t stop PETROS DGO rights fight” tak dapat reach nasional seperti BH, Awani, TV3.[18]
- Jadi kepada penonton nasional, **frame Petronas** dominate; frame Sarawak tenggelam.

## 3. Adakah ini sengaja dari “Petronas side”?

Boleh pecah dua: niat boleh kita agak, tapi kita kena label “Estimate Only”.

- Motif rasional yang **masuk akal** untuk Petronas:  
  - Kurangkan political pressure ke PMX & MOF: kalau media nampak Sarawak asyik kalah, tekanan untuk reform PDA / revenue share jadi perlahan.[19][20][21]
  - Jaga credit rating & investor confidence: dengan menonjolkan kemenangan mahkamah kecil dan “clarity” narrative, mereka cuba lawan impression bahawa Malaysia regulatory environment unstable.[16][22][4]
  - Jaga posisi tawar: perception bahawa DGO challenge lemah meningkatkan leverage Petronas dalam sebarang commercial settlement akan datang.  
- Bukti direct (smoking gun) bahawa Petronas orchestrate media lines → **tiada** dalam sources terbuka. Cannot Compute.  
  - Tapi pattern: statement rasmi Petronas + pick‑up media yang heavy pada quote peguam Petronas **selari** dengan kepentingan reputasi Petronas dan Putrajaya.[15][2][1][12]

Jadi, arifOS view:  
- “Petronas main perception game” = **Estimate Only tapi plausible**, based on alignment of narrative with their interests, bukan based on leak/direct evidence.

- Asimetri kuasa maklumat:  
  - Petronas ada akses ke media nasional, reputasi “teknokrat”, dan boleh shaping narrative “kami hanya ikut undang‑undang”.[15][2][4]

- Governance floor F2 (Truth) & F4 (ΔS):  
  - Naratif sempit ini **kurangkan** kefahaman rakyat tentang akar masalah dan **tingkatkan** kekeliruan (ΔS) – itu failure amanah maklumat, walaupun sah di atas kertas undang‑undang.[21][16]

Dalam bahasa kau: bukan level “tipu data”, tapi level “spin separuh cerita” – secara etika governance, itu memang kira main kotor ringan.

Here’s a version you can more or less drop into a UOB-style note for your friend – you can adjust house views/FX as needed.

***

## 1. Framing the announcement

- Petronas has guided to “about RM2b a year set aside for exploration in the next five years.” [1]
- This sits within a broader plan to “ramp up exploration and production” and maintain domestic output at close to 2m boe/d between 2026–2028 via exploration, deepwater and EOR. [2][3][4]
- Group capex is still large: FY2024 capex was ~RM54.2b (+3% y/y), with domestic capex at RM33.1b (+26% y/y), and the Street expects ~RM50b capex in 2025. [5]

**Analytical punchline:** RM2b exploration is de‑risking and mildly pro‑growth for basin life, but looks under‑powered as a primary growth vector versus Petronas’ balance sheet and the ambition to be a regional energy champion.

***

## 2. Peer benchmarking – exploration “option premium”

### 2.1 Scale vs global majors

Use rough FX RM4.5/USD (you can swap to house FX):

- Petronas exploration: RM2b ≈ USD0.45b p.a. [1]
- ExxonMobil: total capital and exploration expenditures USD27.6b in 2024; historically, exploration runs mid‑single to high‑single‑digit % of upstream capex, implying perhaps USD1.5–2.5b of exploration p.a. (5–10% of upstream). [6][7] (Estimate Only)  
- Rystad data: six upstream majors collectively spent ~USD7b p.a. on exploration in 2020–24. [6]
- NGO dataset: a group of European majors (TotalEnergies, Shell, BP, Eni, Equinor, OMV, etc.) now spend nearly USD8.4b annually on exploration of new fields. [8]

Implied ranking:

- Petronas is running exploration at perhaps one‑quarter to one‑third of the level of an individual supermajor, and a fraction of the European cohort, despite being a systemically important NOC with sizable legacy production. [6][8][1] (Estimate Only)  

### 2.2 Within Petronas’ own capital stack

- FY2024 capex: RM54.2b; expected FY2025 capex ~RM50b. [5]
- If exploration is RM2b, this is ~4% of total capex and an even smaller share of total operating cash flow / profit, given Petronas’ net profit was ~RM26b in 1H 2025 alone. [9][10][5] (Estimate Only)  
- UOB Kay Hian previously flagged that Petronas’ upstream capex (including gas & new energy) was guided to RM32–34b p.a. for five years, implying exploration is <10% of upstream capex. [11]

**Takeaway:** Exploration is being treated as a slim “real option premium” rather than a central capital allocation pillar.

***

## 3. Strategic context – Sarawak, overseas tilt, and domestic basin maturity

- UOBKH has already argued that Sarawak’s Petros taking over as sole gas aggregator is a key driver for Petronas to tilt capex towards overseas projects (e.g., Canada, Argentina), implying domestic upstream capex will be “relatively unexciting.” [12]
- Kenanga notes domestic capex is still rising but warns of potential capex reductions of RM5–10b arising from the Sarawak gas aggregation deal, even if Petronas keeps headline capex in the RM50b region. [5]
- The ETP/OGE NKEA documents highlight that, structurally, Malaysia’s upstream growth over the last decade came more from prices and Petronas’ international expansion than from production volume growth, underscoring maturity of domestic basins. [13][14]

In that context, a modest RM2b exploration line:

- Signals “life‑extension mode” for domestic basins: enough to manage decline and prolong plateau, but not enough to structurally re‑rate reserves and long‑term growth. [2][3][4][1] (Estimate Only)  
- Frees capital for deepwater developments, brownfield/EOR, and overseas growth, consistent with earlier UOBKH commentary on Petronas “going all out on overseas ventures.” [12]

***

## 4. Macro multiplier and GNI lens

You can frame this using old but still useful ETP/PEMANDU coefficients.

### 4.1 ETP ratios

- OGE NKEA roadmap: 12 EPPs plus business opportunities expected to deliver RM131.4b GNI impact by 2020 off substantial upstream and downstream investment. [13][14]
- One cited EOR programme: RM68.6b investment → RM16.6b incremental annual GNI at maturity, implying capital‑output of ~4:1 and GNI/capex of ~0.24 per year once projects are on plateau. [13]
- LNG regasification terminal case: RM3.9b capex → RM0.6b GNI from operation plus broader GNI and savings from fuel switching, again implying material but not explosive multipliers. [13]

### 4.2 Stylised chain for RM2b exploration

A simple stylised chain (flag it as conceptual, not a forecast):

- Step 1 (Finding leverage): Each RM1 of exploration that succeeds tends to catalyse ~5–10x in development capex (seismic → discovery → appraisal → full field). (Estimate Only)  
- Step 2 (Capex to GNI): Use the EOR ratio as a crude proxy: RM1 of upstream development capex → RM0.2–0.25 of incremental annual GNI once fully ramped. [13]
- Step 3 (Macro weight): Malaysia’s nominal GDP is >RM2t today. [15]

Then:

- RM2b exploration → RM10–20b future development → RM2–5b incremental annual GNI at maturity per “cohort” of discoveries. [13] (Estimate Only)  
- As a share of GDP, this is ~0.1–0.25% of GDP per cohort, i.e., supportive but not system‑defining. [13][15] (Estimate Only)  

**Implication for an analyst:** RM2b p.a. exploration is macro‑positive, particularly for Malaysian OGSE order books and related NKEAs, but in macro terms, it is more about “sustaining” the OGE contribution than reproducing the original ETP‑era GNI uplift story. [13][14][5]

***

## 5. Reserve‑replacement and production sustainability (toy framework)

For your friend, you can offer a reserve‑replacement heuristic rather than a full model:

- Suppose long‑run finding & development cost for new barrels is USD10–15/boe on a risked basis in Malaysian basins (mid‑case emerging/developed offshore). (Estimate Only)  
- Petronas wants to hold domestic production “close to 2m boe/d” (≈730m boe/year) over 2026–28. [2][3][4]
- At 730m boe/year, a 100% reserve‑replacement ratio requires booking ~730m boe/year. (Estimate Only)  

If exploration spend is USD0.45b (RM2b) and risked F&D is USD12/boe, **exploration alone could only support ~37m boe/year of new reserves**, i.e., ~5% of current production, with the balance coming from:

- Reserve upgrades in existing fields via EOR/brownfield.  
- Revisions and improved recovery factors.  
- Farm‑ins/acquisitions and overseas projects.  

This quantifies the “option premium” narrative: at current levels, exploration is simply not intended to carry the reserve‑replacement load; it’s one component in a broader field‑life‑extension and external growth strategy. [6][2][3][4][1] (Estimate Only)

***

## 6. Equity/sector angles for a UOB analyst

He might care about how to translate this into sector calls:

- OGSE activity mix:  
  - Exploration spend of RM2b/year plus Petronas guidance of 91–100 wells drilled by 2028 supports continued demand for drilling, seismic and subsea/EPCC, though the cycle is more “steady‑state upcycle” than “super‑cycle”. [3][4][5][1]
  - Plugging & abandonment wells rising from 63 in 2025 to 70–80 by 2028 signal ageing asset base and growing decommissioning market, which benefits certain OSV and EPC names. [3][4]
- Domestic vs overseas tilt:  
  - UOBKH already highlighted Petronas’ greater focus on overseas projects post‑Petros, implying domestic upstream capex growth may lag group capex. [12][11]
  - Domestic OGSE names more leveraged to Petronas’ local capex could see decent but not explosive order flows, whereas globalised players may benefit if Petronas adds more overseas deepwater/FLNG work. [12][5]
- Risk skew:  
  - Policy risk: further evolution of federal–state resource governance (Sarawak/Sabah) could re‑shape where Petronas allocates incremental upstream dollars. [12][5]
  - Energy transition: ETP and National Energy Policy treat oil & gas as a bridge, not an indefinite growth engine; hence capital discipline and limited exploration tilt are consistent with a strategy of harvesting cash to fund downstream, gas and new energy. [13][15][14]

**Message he can carry:** treat the RM2b exploration signal as:

- A confirmation of capex discipline and preference for near‑cashflow projects (brownfield/EOR, deepwater tie‑backs, overseas projects). [2][3][4][5][1]
- A modest positive for OGSE volumes and Malaysia’s OGE GNI, but not a regime shift vs prior expectations. [13][14][5]
- A constraint on long‑term domestic hydrocarbon growth optionality, increasing the importance of international assets and non‑upstream engines in Petronas’ valuation and in Malaysia’s macro‑energy equation. [6][13][12][5][1]

You can tweak numbers to UOB house FX and plug into their preferred valuation/macro template, but structurally this gives him a coherent “capex discipline, overseas tilt, domestic sustain‑not‑transform” narrative around the RM2b figure.
